name: Fullers Bridge
facts: Fullers Bridge, completed in 1918, was the first continuous reinforced concrete girder bridge in New South Wales, showcasing early 20th-century engineering prowess.
The bridge’s octagonal piers, each with a square core and chamfered edges, give it a distinctive, almost castle‑like appearance across the Lane Cove River.
In 1963, the mysterious discovery of Dr Gilbert Bogle and Mrs Margaret Chandler’s bodies 70 metres south of Fullers Bridge added a chilling chapter to Sydney’s local lore.
